meta.showcase_note: Margaret, Harold and Ruth are real pipeline outputs on synthetic test households, renamed to match the pitch.

claims.text: A password reset was made by mobile on 2025-07-10.
A login from a new device on the web followed on 2025-07-12, and a second password reset by phone came later that same day.
An earlier new-device login on the web happened on 2025-05-30.
A $100 check went to a first-time individual payee, Tom Mercer, on 2025-05-16.
A scheduled withdrawal goes to an account that received money from one other client in the last 90 days, and that client was paying it for the first time.
There are no advisor notes in the last 180 days that explain the account changes or the new payee.

cases.name: Margaret Ellis
cases.pattern: Possible investment, crypto or romance scam

claims.text: Margaret asked for the quickest way to move money and did not want to wait for a check.
Margaret described a new 'boyfriend' named Andrew whom she has never met in person.
Margaret said she was instructed not to tell anyone at the bank or the firm.
About $16,490 was requested out in the last 30 days.
Last month Margaret discussed long-term care options at her own request, and no action was taken.

cases.name: Walter Walsh
cases.pattern: Possible investment, crypto or romance scam

claims.text: Walter mentioned a friend he met on Instagram, a woman named Elena.
Wires to 'Federal Clearing Acct', first paid on 2025-05-06, rose from $910 to $4,420 to $7,960 to $14,320 between May 6 and June 7.
Walter said the $14,320 was to pay off old credit cards, but it went by wire to 'Federal Clearing Acct'.
A $500 transfer went to his own checking account; he said it was a wedding gift for a grandchild.
In recent conversations Walter seemed well and engaged: a review meeting, a beneficiary review with no concerns, and questions about CD rates.
Only $680 was requested out in the last 30 days.

cases.name: Harold Brennan
cases.pattern: Possible exploitation by someone close to the client

claims.text: The phone number on the account was changed on 2025-11-07 through the web channel.
A joint owner was added at a branch on 2025-11-12.
The trusted contact was removed by phone on 2025-11-19.
A $5,080 check went to Kelly Brennan, an individual marked as a new payee, on 2025-12-03.
A $6,470 ACH payment went to Kelly Brennan on 2025-12-23, the as-of date.
The $6,470 payment was funded by selling a position held for 15 years.

The scoring reasons describe $11,550 sent in 90 days to a payee who holds a role on the account, after the trusted contact was removed. The reason names the payee 'Kelly Brennan', while the transactions show 'Kelly Brennan'. This name mismatch should be checked.
The scoring reasons note 3 warning signs across 2 engines in the last 30 days.

Advisor notes from July to September describe routine conversations: staying the course, monthly distribution unchanged, comfortable with the current allocation. None mentions plans for large gifts or payments to family.
